papers.summary: In modular-arithmetic models, effective-rank compression follows grokking rather than causing it. Rank caps and a nuclear-norm penalty do not bring generalization forward against factorized controls.
papers.relevance: Direct evidence for interpreting singular-value spectra, effective rank, memorization, and low-rank compressibility during training.

evidence.quote: The steepest fall in effective rank comes about 900 steps after the onset
against a factorized full-rank control, capping W in W_{\text{in}} at rank 32, 24 or 16, all above the 13 directions its solution needs, never lowers the mean onset

papers.title: Subspace Crystallization in Grokking: Rank Compression Tracks the Phase Transition

papers.summary: A pretraining study of fourteen orthogonality variants finds no reliable benefit from network-wide row orthogonality beyond per-row sphere optimization. Sphere optimization improves on tuned Muon in the reported setting.
papers.relevance: Tests whether matrix constraints improve LLM pretraining, with an important distinction from orthogonality claims in LoRA fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: We examine fourteen variants of orthogonality training
no d > 1 d>1 used throughout the network reliably outperforms d = 1 d=1

papers.title: Do Orthogonality Constraints Help Language-Model Training Beyond Sphere Optimization?

papers.summary: ProLand combines coordinated LoRA-factor updates with Muon-style spectral directions and a separate orthogonality-restoring correction. The paper reports the highest task-averaged scores among its compared methods across the tested encoder and decoder model–rank configurations.
papers.relevance: Directly addresses the geometry, optimization, and practical language-model behavior of low-rank adapters.

evidence.quote: The spectral direction is therefore defined at the level of B ​ A BA , rather than independently in the two factor spaces
In the main language evaluations, ProLand achieves the highest task-averaged scores among the compared methods in the encoder setting and all seven decoder model–rank configurations.

papers.title: ProLand: A New Infeasible Manifold Optimization Method for LoRA Fine-Tuning

papers.summary: MuonGS removes the radial component of a Muon update without fixing the weight norm. In 160M and 400M GPT-style pretraining, it reports lower validation perplexity than MuonH at longer horizons and an estimated 7–15% token-equivalent speedup.
papers.relevance: Connects matrix-optimizer geometry and weight-norm control to measured LLM pretraining performance.

evidence.quote: We tune learning rates on a multiplicative grid with ratio 2 \sqrt{2} similar to Wen et al. (2026) , separately for all optimizers, model sizes and training durations.
MuonGS achieves a token-equivalent speedup over MuonH up to about 7-15% for longer training horizons.

papers.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control

papers.summary: Functional Rank Allocation uses end-to-end measurements to distribute retained rank within and across LoRA adapters. At constrained fleet budgets, it improves reported worst-case and tail utility over uniform spectral compression.
papers.relevance: Directly tests whether spectral redundancy predicts functional low-rank compressibility while preserving adapter utility.

evidence.quote: Although trained LoRAs contain substantial spectral redundancy, spectral reconstruction alone does not determine how much compression an adapter can functionally tolerate.
Across 78 adapters from three public fleets, FRA improves worst-case and tail utility over uniform spectral compression in constrained-budget regimes.

papers.title: LoRA on a Budget: Function-Aware Post-Hoc Compression for Adapter Fleets

papers.summary: SimplexLoRA learns a non-uniform adapter-rank allocation under a fixed parameter budget. Its comparisons with standard LoRA show gains across several language tasks and ranks, especially at low ranks.
papers.relevance: A practical study of low-rank fine-tuning quality under matched adapter-capacity constraints.

evidence.quote: SimplexLoRA achieving the best average score at the same 0.24 % 0.24\% parameter budget as standard LoRA
The improvement is most pronounced at low ranks ( r ∈ { 1 , 2 } r\in\{1,2\} )

papers.title: SimplexLoRA: Dynamic Rank Updating via Alternating Minimization with Simplex Projection

papers.summary: Dobb performs matrix-aware optimizer updates within parameter shards. On GPT-2 XL it reports validation loss 2.476 versus Dion’s 2.511 at the stated configurations, and an amortized optimizer-call time of 9.2 ms versus 124.1 ms under FSDP on 32 H100 GPUs.
papers.relevance: Addresses the profile’s quality–communication–compute tradeoff for sharded LLM training; optimizer-call timing should not be read as end-to-end throughput.

evidence.quote: On GPT-2 XL (1.56B parameters), Dobb with 16 blocks reaches a validation loss of 2.476, compared with 2.511 for Dion at rank fraction 1/16.
Under FSDP on 32 H100 GPUs, Dobb reduces the amortized optimizer-call time from 124.1 ms for Dion to 9.2 ms.

papers.title: Dobb: Shard-Local Preconditioning in Block-Diagonal Eigenbases

limitations: No selected paper establishes that low-rank pretraining improves full-model weight compressibility at LLM scale.
The retrieved ProLand passages do not quantify matched peak-memory or training-time costs.

Dobb’s reported optimizer-call timing is not an end-to-end throughput measurement, and its zero cross-shard payload definition excludes forward-backward communication and activation-moment synchronization.
The MuonGS token-equivalent speedup is estimated from a fitted loss-versus-token-budget curve, not measured wall-clock speedup.
